items.title: Discover tools at runtime with AWS Agent Registry
items.abstract: Runtime discovery with AWS Agent Registry can help address a problem that agent demos might hide. Hardcoded tools work fine for a handful, start to degrade at a few dozen, and become unmanageable beyond that. Enterprise systems expose hundreds of internal APIs for pricing, support, orders, inventory, and customer data. In these systems, the model can spend more tokens disambiguating tool names than reasoning about the user’s request. Each new capability requires a code change in the orchestrator, a redeploy, and a coordinated release across teams that would much rather ship on their own cadence. This pattern can arise across enterprise software as a service (SaaS) engagements where teams expose large internal API surfaces to agentic consumers. Build-time wiring can become a bottleneck as the catalog expands. One approach is to change how the orchestrator accesses its tools: instead of compiling every tool into the agent, the agent can discover relevant tools at runtime. AWS Agent Registry is a managed service for cataloging and discovering Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agents, and agent skills. Publishers register protocol-specific descriptors and searchable descriptions. At runtime, an orchestrator can search approved, discoverable records and use the returned endpoint and descriptor content to construct a client. Registry search results do not return the capability’s invocation credentials or authentication scheme. This post walks through the Discover → Instantiate → Execute loop demonstrated by the refactored Python sample. The code deploys an order-management MCP server through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, two agent-to-agent (A2A) agents on AgentCore runtime , a Registry, and an orchestrator. The sample directory contains the deployment script, orchestrator, helper modules, and cleanup script. Solution overview: discover, instantiate, execute The orchestrator agent in this sample has no built-in knowledge of tools or agents. Figure 1: Without AWS Agent Registry (left), endpoints are hardcoded and adding a new agent means code changes plus redeployment. With AWS Agent Registry (right), the orchestrator discovers capabilities through semantic search and new integrations are usable after registration and approval Discover The orchestrator sends a natural-language query to the AWS Agent Registry data plane. The search response includes record identity, name, description, record type, status, version, and protocol descriptors such as MCP server metadata or an A2A agent card. It does not include invocation credentials. The application must obtain and apply the appropriate credentials through a separate, trusted configuration path. Instantiate For each returned record, the orchestrator constructs a client from the descriptor type. In this sample, the registered MCP server represents tools that were first added as targets to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. The MCP descriptor therefore points to the Gateway endpoint. The orchestrator fetches a Cognito OAuth access token separately and uses it when creating the MCPClient . A2A records contain an agent card whose URL identifies an AgentCore runtime endpoint. The wrapper invokes that runtime through the boto3 data-plane client, which signs the request with the caller’s AWS credentials. Registry discovery supplies connection metadata, not the authentication material. Execute An ephemeral inner agent is built with only the dynamically-discovered tools. The large language model (LLM) picks the right one(s) for the request, and the result is synthesized back to the user. After the turn finishes, the inner agent and its clients are torn down. The next request gets a fresh search and a fresh tool set. Figure 2: End-to-end architecture. A single orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime queries AWS Agent Registry. Matched MCP servers are invoked through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, and matched A2A agents are invoked on Ama

items.summary: AWS Agent Registry는 MCP 서버, 에이전트, 에이전트 스킬을 카탈로그화하고 검색할 수 있는 관리형 서비스다. 기존에는 도구를 오케스트레이터에 모두 하드코딩해야 해 수십 개를 넘어가면 관리가 어렵고, 새 기능 추가마다 코드 변경과 재배포, 팀 간 조율된 릴리스가 필요했다. 이 글은 Discover → Instantiate → Execute 루프를 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, A2A 에이전트, Registry, 오케스트레이터로 구성된 Python 샘플로 설명한다. 오케스트레이터는 자연어 쿼리로 Registry를 검색해 레코드 식별자, 설명, MCP/A2A 디스크립터를 받지만 **인증 자격 증명은 별도 경로로 획득**해야 한다. 매 요청마다 동적으로 발견된 도구만으로 임시 내부 에이전트를 구성하고 처리 후 폐기한다.
items.why_it_matters: 수백 개의 내부 API를 노출하는 엔터프라이즈 시스템에서는 도구 이름 구분에 토큰을 낭비하거나 배포 병목이 발생하는데, **런타임 도구 발견**은 이런 빌드타임 결합 문제를 완화할 수 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 하드코딩된 오케스트레이터(모든 도구를 사전 컴파일하는 방식) 대비, Registry 기반 검색으로 승인된 레코드를 런타임에 조회하고 엔드포인트만으로 클라이언트를 동적으로 구성한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
items.abstract: Most large language models (LLMs) use transformer architectures with softmax attention. During inference, their key-value (KV) cache grows with the conversation or document context. This can reduce concurrency, increase serving cost, and force agentic applications to discard useful history. i14 designed Laplace 3B as a linear attention alternative. Its recurrent state stays at 29.5 MB per sequence, independent of context length. Working with AWS, i14 used native PyTorch support through TorchNeuron Native to bring this custom architecture to AWS Trainium2 . This preserved its Gated Linear Attention (GLA) design and Muon optimizer. On one trn2.48xlarge instance, Laplace 3B trained at about 120,000 tokens per second. The model served 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences. This post explains the model design, the changes i14 made for Trainium2, and the training and inference results. About i14 i14 is an AI research and technology company that develops model architectures, components, and runtimes. Its work draws on AI, computational cognitive science, and research into how biological systems learn over time. i14 applies these ideas to models that can retain long-range context without allowing serving state to grow with every token. Why linear attention models? Transformer softmax attention compares tokens across the context. During training, this computation grows quadratically with sequence length. During inference, the KV cache grows as the model processes more tokens. Linear attention reorganizes the computation around a recurrent state that is updated for each token. Laplace 3B uses GLA to compress prior context into a fixed-size matrix state. This changes training attention from O( T 2) to O( T ) and keeps inference state fixed at 29.5 MB per sequence. Consideration Transformer softmax attention Laplace 3B with GLA Training attention Builds pairwise token scores with O( T 2) scaling Updates chunked recurrent state with O( T ) scaling Inference memory KV cache grows with context Recurrent state remains fixed in size Longer contexts Each sequence consumes more accelerator memory Context length does not increase recurrent-state allocation Implementation Uses widely optimized attention kernels Requires architecture-specific kernels and compiler tuning Linear attention compresses history rather than retaining every key and value. You must therefore evaluate retrieval quality for your workloads. The fixed state can benefit long-running agents, large-document analysis, and applications that need persistent memory with predictable serving requirements. How i14 adapted Laplace 3B for AWS Trainium2 The original implementation of Laplace 3B used GPU-optimized Triton kernels. The AWS Generative AI Innovation Center (GenAIIC) team first rewrote the GLA kernel with standard PyTorch operators for Trainium2. After comparing both approaches, the team chose the beta version of TorchNeuron Native, the native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium , because it performed better. The implementation required three changes: Using native PyTorch for the GLA attention kernel. The team replaced the GPU-specific fused_chunk_simple_gla Triton kernel with standard PyTorch operators, using 16 chunks of 128 tokens to match the 128 partitions of the NeuronCore on-chip buffer. Redesigning how Muon communicates. Two all_to_all collectives in MuonFSDP2 cut per-rank traffic by 24 times and raised throughput by 1.63 times. Compiling the sequential backward pass. The team statically unrolled the 16 chunk steps of the GLA recurrence to fit the graph-size and on-chip memory limits of the compiler. The engineering challenges section describes each change in detail. Why AWS Trainium accelerators? AWS Trainium is a family of AWS machine learning (ML) accelerators designed for model training and inference. A trn2.48xlarge instance combines 16 Trainium2 chips, 64 logical NeuronCores, high-bandwidth memory, and NeuronLink-v3 connectivity. These resou

items.summary: i14는 트랜스포머의 KV 캐시 증가 문제를 해결하기 위해 Gated Linear Attention(GLA) 기반의 Laplace 3B 모델을 설계했다. 이 모델은 컨텍스트 길이와 무관하게 시퀀스당 **29.5MB의 고정 크기 재귀 상태**만 유지한다. AWS와 협력해 GPU용 Triton 커널을 표준 PyTorch 연산으로 재작성하고, TorchNeuron Native 백엔드를 통해 Trainium2에 이식했으며 GLA 구조와 Muon 옵티마이저를 유지했다. trn2.48xlarge 인스턴스 1대에서 초당 약 12만 토큰으로 학습했고, 1,280개 동시 시퀀스에서 **초당 11,544개 출력 토큰**을 서빙했다.
items.why_it_matters: KV 캐시 증가는 긴 대화나 문서를 다루는 에이전트 애플리케이션의 동시성과 비용에 직접적인 제약이 되는데, 고정 크기 상태를 가진 선형어텐션은 이 한계를 구조적으로 해소할 수 있다는 점에서 장기 실행 에이전트와 대용량 문서 분석에 의미가 크다.
items.whats_different: 기존 소프트맥스 어텐션의 학습 연산이 O(T²)로 증가하고 추론 시 **KV 캐시가 컨텍스트에 비례해 커지는 것** 대비, Laplace 3B는 GLA로 학습을 O(T)로 줄이고 추론 상태를 고정 크기로 유지하며, GPU 전용 Triton 커널 대신 표준 PyTorch 연산과 all_to_all 통신 재설계, 역전파 그래프 정적 언롤링으로 Trainium2에 맞게 이식했다.

items.title: Work management context for AI agents with Smartsheet MCP on AWS
items.abstract: AI agents are most useful when they can act on the real work happening across your organization. Work management involves complex, cross-functional tasks such as updating project timelines, reassigning tasks, and surfacing status. AI agents can support you with these without anyone switching tools. Smartsheet , the work management platform for managing projects, portfolios, and operations, has launched a generally available Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server. With the Smartsheet MCP Server , AI assistants can read, write, and manage Smartsheet data through a standardized protocol. The protocol spans more than 40 tools for exploring, creating, and managing sheets, rows, columns, and automations. You can update task statuses, create rows, and modify project structure directly through natural language. In this post, we walk through two ways you can connect it to your existing workflows. Amazon Quick is an agentic AI workspace built for business users, project managers, and operations teams. They can ask questions, update sheets, and build dashboards through natural language without writing code. Kiro is an agentic IDE where developers connect to Smartsheet through MCP to reference project specs, update task status, and track dependencies without leaving their coding workflow. Architecture overview The following diagram shows how the Smartsheet MCP Server sits as the central integration layer connecting to AWS services. Amazon Quick and Kiro connect directly as MCP clients. Amazon Quick serves knowledge workers, project managers, and operations teams who want to query, update, and automate Smartsheet through natural language. With Kiro, developers can reference project specs, update task status, and track dependencies without leaving their coding workflow. The following architecture diagram illustrates these integration paths: the Smartsheet MCP Server in the center, with Amazon Quick and Kiro as MCP clients on the left, and Smartsheet’s API and data layer on the right. Figure 1: Smartsheet MCP Server architecture showing MCP client connections from Amazon Quick and Kiro through the server to the Smartsheet API layer Sprint management with Amazon Quick and Kiro Consider a software engineering team that tracks their sprint in Smartsheet. Tasks, owners, statuses, and blockers all live in a project sheet. Here’s what each path looks like for the same team: When a user such as a project manager wants to check which sprint tasks are blocked this week, they can ask Amazon Quick through natural language. The Amazon Quick chat agent queries the Smartsheet MCP Server, pulls the relevant rows, and surfaces a summary with owner names and due dates. The response is generated from live Smartsheet data without building a report or dashboard. For developers who are fixing bugs or working through features, they can ask Kiro to pull the current sprint sheet and show them the open backend tasks assigned to them. Kiro queries Smartsheet through MCP and surfaces the list inline. When the fix is committed, a Kiro hook automatically updates the corresponding row status to Complete. Prerequisites Smartsheet MCP Server delivers precisely structured context, including row relationships, column types, cell history, and comments. This produces token-efficient payload sizes rather than returning raw API payloads. This engineering decision compounds into reduced cost and improved latency at scale when running hundreds of AI-assisted queries across a project portfolio. To learn how Smartsheet built their remote MCP server on AWS, see How Smartsheet built a remote MCP server on AWS . Before connecting the Smartsheet MCP Server to Amazon Quick and Kiro, verify that you have the following in place: An active AWS account with appropriate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions for the service you’re connecting (Amazon Quick, or Kiro) A Smartsheet account on a Business, Enterprise, or AWM plan. A Smartsheet Personal Access Token, or OAuth credentials

items.title: Securing AI agent identity with X.509 PKI on AWS
items.abstract: When AI agents access databases, APIs, and sensitive business operations, establishing cryptographic identity through X.509 public key infrastructure (PKI) becomes a critical requirement. The core challenge is proving which agent made a request, preventing forgery between agents, and confirming that each agent acts only on behalf of an authorized user. Traditional approaches such as sharing API keys between components or passing OAuth tokens through agent chains fall short of the zero-trust requirements that enterprise deployments demand. Multi-agent AI frameworks increasingly use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect agents to external tools and data sources. MCP defines how a large language model (LLM)-powered agent invokes tools such as database queries or email operations. However, MCP has no built-in authentication standard. It is transport-agnostic by design. This creates a critical gap: Without proper identity mechanisms, any component could impersonate an agent, replay intercepted credentials, or invoke tools without authorization. In this post, we show you how to address this gap using Keyfactor EJBCA combined with AWS services. EJBCA is a PKI platform that supports high-availability deployment, REST API automation, and Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) validation. The reference architecture uses four complementary security mechanisms. First, signed request envelopes provide cryptographic proof-of-possession on every agent call. Second, user-signed delegation assertions authorize agents without sharing credentials. Third, RFC 8693 audience-scoped tokens limit the scope of exposure from any single token disclosure. Fourth, real-time OCSP revocation checking propagates credential changes immediately across all agents. The solution uses Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference through the AWS Strands Agents SDK . While this reference architecture uses a database as the protected resource, the same authentication pattern applies to any MCP-compatible tool server. Complete source code for all examples is available in the accompanying GitHub repository. About Keyfactor EJBCA Keyfactor provides a widely adopted machine identity management platform used by more than 1,500 enterprise customers worldwide, according to Keyfactor. These organizations span financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, and government. Keyfactor helps organizations establish and maintain cryptographic trust through certificate lifecycle management, PKI operations, and machine identity governance. EJBCA Enterprise is Keyfactor’s Certificate Authority (CA) and PKI platform, designed for high-availability deployment and REST API automation. Available as an enterprise product, EJBCA provides X.509 certificate issuance, OCSP validation, certificate revocation list (CRL) distribution, and full certificate lifecycle management through both a web console and REST API. EJBCA supports deployment on-premises, in containers, or on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2). The partnership between AWS and Keyfactor brings together AWS managed services (Amazon Bedrock, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)) with PKI infrastructure that supports certificate lifecycle management, automated enrollment, and real-time revocation. This combination addresses a gap in the AI agent ecosystem. While AWS provides the compute, storage, and AI inference layers, Keyfactor provides the cryptographic identity layer that binds agents to verifiable, revocable, short-lived credentials. This joint reference architecture, developed collaboratively by the AWS and Keyfactor engineering teams, demonstrates how to integrate these technologies. You can adapt the patterns shown here to your own multi-agent deployments. items.title_ko: AWS·Keyfactor, X.509 PKI로 AI 에이전트 신원 인증 — MCP의 인증 공백 메운다
items.summary: AI 에이전트가 DB·API 등 민감한 작업에 접근할 때 요청자를 증명하고 위조를 막기 위해 X.509 PKI 기반 암호화 신원 체계가 필요하다고 설명한다. 멀티 에이전트 프레임워크가 널리 쓰는 Model Context Protocol(MCP)은 전송 방식에 독립적으로 설계되어 **인증 표준이 내장되어 있지 않다**는 공백이 있다. 이를 메우기 위해 AWS는 Keyfactor EJBCA와 결합한 참조 아키텍처를 제시하며, 서명된 요청 봉투, 사용자 서명 위임 승인, RFC 8693 기반 범위 제한 토큰, 실시간 OCSP 폐기 확인 등 네 가지 보안 메커니즘을 사용한다. 솔루션은 Amazon Bedrock과 AWS Strands Agents SDK로 LLM 추론을 수행하며, DB를 보호 대상 리소스로 삼지만 동일 인증 패턴을 모든 MCP 호환 도구 서버에 적용할 수 있다.
items.why_it_matters: 다중 에이전트 시스템이 외부 도구·데이터에 접근하는 구조가 보편화되면서, 인증 표준이 없는 MCP의 보안 공백은 에이전트 가장·토큰 재생·무단 도구 호출 같은 실제 위협으로 이어질 수 있다. 엔터프라이즈가 제로트러스트 요건을 만족시키며 AI 에이전트를 운영하려면 이런 암호화 신원 계층 설계가 선행 과제가 된다.
items.whats_different: API 키 공유나 OAuth 토큰을 에이전트 체인에 그대로 전달하는 **기존 방식 대비**, 서명 기반 proof-of-possession과 사용자 서명 위임, 범위 제한 토큰, 실시간 폐기 확인을 결합해 자격 증명 노출과 위조 위험을 줄인다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: How Octave built a secure multi-tenant AI foundation on Amazon Bedrock
items.abstract: In quality management for regulated industries, the institutional memory that resolves a problem is almost always buried somewhere in a customer’s history. A similar defect investigated last year, a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) that fixed the root cause, an audit finding that flagged the same gap. That knowledge sits in billions of documents no human can search by semantic similarity across languages and formats, so every investigation starts from scratch. Octave Reliance has helped each organization collect documents across multiple systems to help them search more easily and keep track of everything they have. The Octave Reliance team saw unlocking this history as its single largest opportunity to help customers work faster and stay compliant. The obstacle was equally clear: complaint records, audit findings, and corrective actions carry the platform’s strictest isolation requirements, and those were exactly the records the AI would need to read. In a platform serving over 14,000 customers across medical devices, pharmaceuticals, and food manufacturing, a single inadvertent disclosure from one customer to another would carry regulatory consequences far outweighing any AI benefit. Octave operates across 180 countries, serving more than 60% of the Global Fortune 500 . Its cloud-native quality management system, Reliance , supports over 650 enterprise customers with over 40 applications, from complaint management and CAPA tracking to audit management and supplier quality. Everyone generates regulated data that AI could reason over. Each customer is a separate tenant and no data can cross a tenant boundary. Faced with that, the Reliance team made an unusual call: rather than shipping one AI feature, it spent its first cycle building a foundation every future feature would sit on. That foundation has since cut deployment time per use case by 50 percent. If you are bringing AI to a software as a service (SaaS) platform where the data is valuable, but isolation is non-negotiable, the reasoning travels beyond quality management. In this post, we walk through the four tensions that shaped the design and the three-layer foundation Octave built with Cohere Embed v4 on Amazon Bedrock. We then follow the pipeline that embedded 2 billion documents and the Complaint Triage Assistant that proved it in production. Why a foundation, not a feature Envisioning workshops with AWS surfaced four high-impact use cases: complaint summarization and triage, audit readiness monitoring, incident narrative generation, and predictive quality risk scoring. They also surfaced the insight that shaped everything after dozens of applications, each with different document types and workflows. Building AI for one in a silo meant rebuilding the infrastructure for the next. So, the team inverted the plan: build the horizontal platform first, then cut vertical feature slices into it. Complaint summarization and triage went first, to prove the architecture before the rest followed. The four tensions Before selecting a single model, the team spent its time on four problems that pulled in different directions. None could be traded away. Making data available without risking inadvertent disclosure. Complaint records, CAPAs, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and audit findings belong to one tenant and must be unreachable by another. Not even an errant AI query could cross. Vector store, retrieval logic, and generation context all had to be scoped to a single tenant. Executing agents in isolation. The permissions governing an agent’s tools, data stores, and model endpoints had to be scoped to the requesting user rather than a shared service role, available only during execution, and respectful of that user’s access rights. A shared agent pool with static credentials failed all three. Reading content that cannot be trusted. items.title_ko: Octave, Amazon Bedrock·Cohere Embed v4로 1만4천 고객사 격리 유지하며 20억 문서 임베딩 — 배포 시간 50% 단축
items.summary: 규제 산업용 품질관리 플랫폼 Reliance를 운영하는 Octave는 고객별 불만 기록, CAPA, 감사 결과 등 민감 데이터를 AI가 활용하되 테넌트 간 격리를 절대 깨뜨리지 않는 기반을 구축했다. 단일 기능 대신 **모든 향후 AI 기능이 올라갈 3계층 공통 플랫폼**을 먼저 만들었고, Cohere Embed v4를 Amazon Bedrock에서 사용해 20억 개 문서를 임베딩했다. 벡터 저장소, 검색 로직, 생성 컨텍스트 모두 테넌트 단위로 범위를 제한했고, 에이전트 권한도 공유 서비스 역할이 아닌 요청 사용자 기준으로 실행 중에만 부여되도록 설계했다. 이 기반 위에서 Complaint Triage Assistant를 실제 프로덕션에 적용해 아키텍처를 검증했다. 그 결과 사용 사례별 **배포 시간이 50% 단축**됐다.
items.why_it_matters: 14,000개 이상 고객사가 의료기기·제약·식품 제조 분야 규제 데이터를 공유하는 멀티테넌트 SaaS에서 AI를 도입할 때, 데이터 유출 하나가 기능 이점을 훨씬 능가하는 규제 리스크로 이어질 수 있음을 보여준다. 격리가 타협 불가한 환경에서 AI를 설계해야 하는 모든 SaaS 사업자에게 적용 가능한 아키텍처 참고 사례다.
items.whats_different: 기능 단위로 AI를 개별 구축하던 기존 방식 대신, 수십 개 애플리케이션에 걸친 **공통 수평 플랫폼을 먼저 구축한 뒤 수직 기능을 끼워 넣는** 방식을 택했으며, 공유 서비스 역할 기반 정적 권한 대신 요청 사용자 범위로 실행 중에만 활성화되는 에이전트 권한 모델을 적용했다.

items.title: Franchisee reconciles cash in 94% less time with ChatGPT Work
items.abstract: An independent Schlotzsky’s and Cinnabon franchisee cut menu repricing time by 95% and built a workflow that could free up $100K in cash flow.
items.title_ko: ChatGPT Work 도입한 프랜차이즈, 현금 정산 시간 94%·메뉴 가격 조정 95% 단축
items.summary: Schlotzsky's와 Cinnabon을 운영하는 한 독립 프랜차이즈 가맹점이 ChatGPT Work를 도입해 업무 효율을 크게 높였다. 메뉴 가격 재조정 작업 시간을 **95% 단축**했고, 현금 정산 작업 시간도 94% 줄였다. 이를 통해 구축한 워크플로우는 최대 10만 달러의 현금 흐름을 확보할 수 있는 것으로 나타났다.
items.why_it_matters: 대규모 조직이 아닌 소규모 프랜차이즈 가맹점에서도 AI 도구로 반복적 재무·운영 업무를 자동화해 실질적인 현금 흐름 개선 효과를 낼 수 있음을 보여주는 사례다.

items.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
items.abstract: We ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating t tokens. Consider two different prompts followed by the same continuation text, so that any difference in their hidden states comes from the prompt alone, and we find that the distance between their hidden states decays approximately as a power law t^{-α}, where α=1 is the rate at which a fixed prompt's share of uniform attention shrinks and smaller values mean longer memory. Trained models forget fast (αapprox0.55--0.7), untrained ones slowly (αapprox0.2--0.5). We prove that this offset is Obig(P(log t)^{L-1}/tbig) for a prompt of length P and depth L. The bound holds for finite-depth pre-LN softmax transformers with bounded attention logits, under one additional condition: the pre-norm activations stay away from zero. The mechanism is geometric: the prompt's direct influence is diluted as the context grows, and relay --- continuation tokens passing on what earlier tokens read from the prompt --- can only add logarithmic factors. This is what we call the conditional no-hair theorem: given the text generated so far, the prompt's influence on the next token vanishes as t grows, so any property of the prompt that survives, such as its language, must be carried by the text itself. An exactly solvable linear relay model shows that the bound cannot be improved and reproduces the rise of the local exponent towards 1 seen in untrained networks. Cancelling the dilution with a logit bias stops the decay early in training and reverses it after, so dilution is necessary for the forgetting we measure; untrained networks and the solvable model show it is also sufficient.
items.title_ko: 트랜스포머의 '조건부 무모론': 생성 토큰 t개 늘수록 프롬프트 영향력 t^-α로 소멸, 학습모델 α≈0.55-0.7
items.summary: 자기회귀 트랜스포머가 같은 이어쓰기 텍스트를 생성할 때, 서로 다른 두 프롬프트의 영향이 히든 상태에서 얼마나 남는지를 분석했다. 두 프롬프트 간 히든 상태 거리는 생성 토큰 수 t에 대해 대략 거듭제곱 법칙 t^-α로 감소하며, **학습된 모델은 α≈0.55-0.7로 빠르게 잊고** 학습되지 않은 모델은 α≈0.2-0.5로 느리게 잊는다. 저자들은 프롬프트 길이 P와 깊이 L에 대해 이 차이가 O(P(log t)^{L-1}/t)로 상한이 잡힌다는 것을 유한 깊이 pre-LN softmax 트랜스포머에서 증명했다. 메커니즘은 기하학적으로, 문맥이 커질수록 프롬프트의 직접 영향이 희석되고, 이전 토큰이 읽은 프롬프트 정보를 전달하는 '릴레이'는 로그 배수만 추가할 수 있다. 정확히 풀리는 선형 릴레이 모델로 이 상한이 개선 불가능함을 보이고, 로짓 바이어스로 희석을 상쇄하면 망각이 멈추거나 역전되어 **희석이 망각의 필요충분조건**임을 확인했다.
items.why_it_matters: 긴 문맥에서 모델이 초기 프롬프트(시스템 지시, 페르소나 등)를 왜 서서히 잊는지에 대한 이론적 근거를 제공해, 장문 생성이나 긴 대화에서의 지시 따르기 저하 문제를 설명하는 데 도움이 된다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 경험적 관찰에 그쳤던 '긴 문맥에서 지시를 잊는다'는 현상을 pre-LN softmax 트랜스포머에 대한 수학적 증명과 해석 가능한 선형 릴레이 모델로 뒷받침했다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Hugging Face ❤️ TorchTPU: TPUs, Natively
items.title_ko: Hugging Face, TorchTPU 공개 — TPU 네이티브 지원 추가
items.summary: Hugging Face가 TorchTPU라는 이름으로 TPU를 네이티브 지원하는 기능을 발표했다. 구체적인 기술 내용은 원문에 제공되지 않았다.
items.why_it_matters: TPU 지원 확대는 Hugging Face 생태계 사용자들의 학습·추론 인프라 선택지에 영향을 줄 수 있다.

items.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
items.abstract: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories. KronLSTM extends the xLSTM family with a memory-revision mechanism that corrects targeted associations while modifying the memory only along a single direction in matrix space. This minimally invasive memory revision reduces interference with previously stored information compared with delta-rule updates, making it particularly well suited for long-context language modeling. The resulting memory dynamics can be mathematically described as a Markov chain that converges to a steady-state distribution, while the expected norm of the memory matrix remains uniformly bounded throughout the entire input sequence. Hence, KronLSTM ensures stable memory dynamics without requiring additional normalization and stabilization mechanisms for the memory state. Experiments show that KronLSTM is competitive with, and often outperforms, existing linear attention architectures, including models of the (Gated) DeltaNet family, with particularly strong performance on long context benchmarks. These results establish the Kronecker Delta Rule as an effective and analytically tractable foundation for stable associative memory in recurrent linear attention architectures. Our code (https://github.com/NX-AI/KronLSTM) and models (https://huggingface.co/collections/NX-AI/kronlstm) are open-source.
items.title_ko: KronLSTM 공개 — Kronecker Delta Rule로 장문맥 선형 어텐션 안정화, DeltaNet 계열 능가
items.summary: 연구진은 연상 행렬 메모리를 위한 새로운 갱신 규칙인 Kronecker Delta Rule을 제안하고, 이를 xLSTM 계열에 적용한 KronLSTM을 제시했다. 이 규칙은 행렬 공간의 단일 방향으로만 메모리를 수정하여 기존 저장된 정보와의 간섭을 최소화하는 **메모리 수정 메커니즘**을 특징으로 한다. 메모리 동역학은 정상 분포로 수렴하는 마르코프 체인으로 수학적으로 기술되며, 메모리 행렬의 기대 노름이 입력 시퀀스 전체에서 균일하게 유계임이 증명되어 별도의 정규화 없이도 안정적이다. 실험 결과 KronLSTM은 (Gated) DeltaNet 계열을 포함한 기존 선형 어텐션 아키텍처와 경쟁력이 있거나 이를 능가하며, 특히 **장문맥 벤치마크**에서 강한 성능을 보였다.
items.why_it_matters: 선형 어텐션의 고질적 문제인 메모리 안정성과 간섭 문제를 별도의 정규화 장치 없이 이론적으로 해결했다는 점에서, 장문맥 언어 모델링을 위한 효율적 아키텍처 설계에 실질적 지침을 제공한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 델타 규칙(DeltaNet) 기반 갱신이 메모리 전체를 수정하는 것과 달리, Kronecker Delta Rule은 행렬 공간의 단일 방향으로만 최소 침습적으로 메모리를 수정해 이전 정보와의 간섭을 줄인다.

items.title: Measuring Mechanistic Uncertainty in Large Language Models via Causal Robustness
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in critical domains, where their susceptibility to hallucinations makes reliable and interpretable uncertainty quantification essential. We introduce the concept of mechanistic uncertainty, which characterizes uncertainty through the stability of the internal mechanisms supporting a model's response. We propose the causal robustness margin, defined as the minimum internal intervention required to deviate the model's output, and operationalize it using Jacobian Lens (Jlens) concept steering vectors. Across three open-source models and five question-answering datasets, we show incorrect and uncertain responses exhibit smaller margins, indicating greater sensitivity to internal interventions, and the causal robustness margin complements conventional output-based uncertainty methods. Finally, in a controlled knowledge injection experiment, correctly learned facts show increased margins after training, suggesting that causal robustness provides a mechanistically grounded signal of uncertainty.
items.title_ko: LLM 내부 메커니즘 안정성으로 불확실성 측정 — '인과적 강건성 마진' 제안, 오답일수록 마진 작아
items.summary: 이 연구는 모델 응답을 뒷받침하는 내부 메커니즘의 안정성으로 불확실성을 정의하는 '메커니즘적 불확실성' 개념을 제안한다. 핵심 지표인 인과적 강건성 마진은 모델 출력을 바꾸는 데 필요한 최소한의 내부 개입 크기로 정의되며, Jacobian Lens(Jlens) 개념 조향 벡터로 측정한다. 3개 오픈소스 모델과 5개 질의응답 데이터셋 실험 결과, **오답 및 불확실한 응답일수록 마진이 작아** 내부 개입에 더 민감함을 보였고, 이는 기존 출력 기반 불확실성 지표를 보완했다. 또한 지식 주입 실험에서 올바르게 학습된 사실은 학습 후 마진이 커져, 인과적 강건성이 메커니즘에 근거한 불확실성 신호임을 시사했다.
items.why_it_matters: LLM 환각 문제 해결을 위해 출력 확률에만 의존하던 불확실성 추정을 모델 내부 구조 관점에서 보완할 수 있어, 고위험 도메인에서 신뢰도 평가의 해석 가능성을 높일 잠재력이 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존 출력 기반(output-based) 불확실성 정량화 방법과 달리, 내부 개입에 대한 민감도를 측정하는 **인과적 강건성 마진**을 도입해 두 접근이 상호 보완적임을 보였다.

items.title: ALTK-Evolve: How learned memory tops the τ²-bench leaderboard on customer service tasks without a frontier model
items.title_ko: ALTK-Evolve, τ²-bench 고객서비스 리더보드 상위권 차지 — 프론티어 모델 없이 학습된 메모리 활용
items.summary: ALTK-Evolve라는 시스템이 학습된 메모리 방식을 사용해 τ²-bench 고객서비스 과제 리더보드에서 상위 성적을 거뒀다는 내용이다.
items.why_it_matters: 프론티어 모델 없이도 높은 성능을 낼 수 있다는 점은 비용 효율적인 AI 시스템 설계에 시사점을 줄 수 있다.

items.title: Synthetic-to-Real Transfer with Frozen DINOv3 Features
items.abstract: Training models on procedurally generated datasets for card detection and segmentation The post Synthetic-to-Real Transfer with Frozen DINOv3 Features appeared first on Towards Data Science .
items.title_ko: 카드 검출·분할, 합성 데이터 학습 후 고정된 DINOv3 특징으로 실사 전이
items.summary: 이 글은 절차적으로 생성된 합성 데이터셋을 이용해 카드 검출 및 분할 모델을 학습시키는 방법을 다룬다. 핵심은 **DINOv3**의 사전학습된 특징을 고정(frozen)한 채로 활용해, 합성 데이터로 학습한 모델이 실제 이미지에도 잘 전이되도록 하는 접근이다. 즉 합성(synthetic) 환경에서 학습한 표현을 실제(real) 도메인으로 옮기는 synthetic-to-real transfer 문제를 다룬다.
items.why_it_matters: 실제 라벨링 데이터 확보가 어려운 검출·분할 과제에서, 합성 데이터와 강력한 사전학습 특징을 결합하면 데이터 수집 비용을 크게 줄일 수 있다는 점에서 실무적 시사점이 크다.

items.title: The Second-User Test
items.abstract: In my work with G7–G12 students at Force Academy, a research initiative in Chongqing, I sometimes take a project that appears to be finished and give another student responsibility for using, checking, or modifying it. The handoff is a test of understanding: Can the work still make sense when its creator is no longer there to translate it? The original author knows what every variable means, why a particular decision was made, which tool was used, and which parts can safely be changed. The second student has only what the project makes visible. Generative AI makes the handoff more revealing because it lowers the cost of producing a convincing first version. Students can generate code, analysis, prose, visualizations, and prototypes far more quickly than they could a few years ago. In a classroom, however, a project is useful only insofar as it shows what the student understands and can defend. AI can supply missing code, smooth over incomplete reasoning, or turn a rough idea into fluent prose, so polish is no longer strong evidence of understanding by itself. A concrete example came from a student paper on AI and labor economics, Verification Responsibility in AI-Applicable Occupations. The paper asked what remains economically important when AI makes candidate outputs cheap but a person still has to check those outputs, decide whether they are safe to use, and remain responsible for accepting them. The lead student developed the conceptual model and most of the analytical workflow. A second student was given a narrower job: rerun the main analyses independently, record the versions of the source data, document how occupations in one dataset were linked to occupations in another, and compare the reported tables and figures with the underlying outputs. What looked like procedural verification quickly became a substantive review of the study. The first problem was reproducibility. The analysis ran on the original machine, but too much of the workflow depended on choices that lived in one student’s memory. To reproduce it elsewhere, the team had to record the data transformations, write down the rules for linking occupational datasets, and keep intermediate results so another person could see how the final numbers had been produced rather than simply rerunning a script and trusting the output. The more consequential problem was in the measurement design. An early version of the study used some of the same autonomy and leadership survey items in two different measures: verification responsibility and adaptive capacity. The software had calculated the relationship between those measures correctly, but part of the apparent relationship could have been created by the fact that the two measures shared some of the same inputs. In other words, the code was doing what it had been asked to do; the question was whether the quantities being compared had been defined cleanly enough. The team rebuilt the measures so they no longer shared survey items, removed ambiguous items, and revised the workflow so source versions, cross-dataset links, exclusions, intermediate files, and reported results could be traced. Later versions added alternative specifications and robustness checks. What began as “please rerun this” ended up forcing a redesign of the study. The handoff changed how I read student work. A second user does not merely test whether the files have been packaged neatly; they ask the awkward questions the creator may have stopped noticing. Why is a particular variable there? Which conclusion depends on an assumption that was never made explicit? In this project, those questions reached back into the measurement design. The educational value of the handoff comes from the fact that schoolwork and production software have different ends. Professional developers learn a great deal after software leaves their hands because they have to deliver it, explain it, support it, maintain it, and respond when someone uses it in an unexpected way. items.title_ko: ‘세컨드 유저 테스트’ — 다른 학생이 재현·검증하자 AI 생성 연구 설계 결함 드러나
items.summary: 저자는 중국 충칭 Force Academy에서 학생이 완성한 프로젝트를 다른 학생에게 넘겨 재현·검증·수정하게 하는 ‘핸드오프’ 방식을 교육에 활용한다. AI 노동경제학 논문 사례에서, 주도 학생이 모델과 분석을 만든 뒤 다른 학생이 독립적으로 분석을 재실행하고 데이터 버전·연결 규칙을 검증하도록 했다. 그 과정에서 재현성 문제(워크플로가 한 학생의 기억에 의존)와 더 심각한 측정 설계 문제(두 지표가 **같은 설문 문항을 공유**해 상관관계가 왜곡됨)가 드러났다. 결국 팀은 지표를 재구성하고 모호한 항목을 제거했으며, 데이터 추적이 가능하도록 전체 분석 과정을 재설계했다.
items.why_it_matters: 생성형 AI로 그럴듯한 초안을 값싸게 만들 수 있게 되면서, **완성도 높은 결과물이 곧 이해를 증명하지 않는다**는 점이 교육과 실무 모두에서 중요한 문제로 떠오른다. 제3자가 재현·검증하는 절차는 AI 지원 작업의 숨은 가정과 설계 결함을 드러내는 실질적 품질 검증 장치가 될 수 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 코드 실행 여부나 결과물 포장 상태를 확인하는 단순 재현 테스트와 달리, 이 핸드오프 방식은 **측정 지표 설계 자체의 타당성**까지 검토하게 만들어 절차적 검증을 실질적 연구 재설계로 이어지게 한다.
